speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To begin our evaluation of your neck swelling, how long has this mass been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, pain, or texture?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Cervical Lymph Nodes.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a two-month history of painless, progressively enlarging swelling on the nape of his neck. Given his significant history of colon cancer (colectomy at age 43), diabetes, and hypertension, this presentation is highly suspicious for a metastatic lymph node. I am requesting a CT scan of the neck and chest to evaluate the extent of the disease. REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck_Chest
